look.why: A bright sunlit reef yellow that harmonizes with the golden ochre body while letting the electric cyan rings glow.

size.measure: mantle length ~5 cm, total length with arms 10–12 cm

habitat.text: Shallow coral reefs, tide pools, and rubble flats across northern Australia, Indonesia, and the Coral Triangle.

diet.text: Small crabs, hermit crabs, and shrimp hunted at night on reef flats.

facts.text: Flashes around 50 to 60 iridescent blue rings in a fraction of a second as a warning display when threatened.
Carries symbiotic bacteria that produce tetrodotoxin, a potent neurotoxin over 1,000 times stronger than cyanide.
